summary: Ramaranjan Mukherji (1928–2010) was an Indologist. He earned his BA and PhD at the University of Calcutta and a DLitt at Jadavpur University. He served as vice chancellor of the University of Burdwan and Rabindra Bharati University.
Ramashastri Bhagavatacharya was an Indology scholar. In 1891, he was attested as an assistant professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as a teacher at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi.

Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist. He served as Professor of Samskrta at Gujarat Vidyapith, with posts also attested in 1938 at L. D. Arts College and S. L. U. Arts and H. & P. Thakore Commerce College for Women.

Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar (1909–2001) was an Indologist who earned an MA at the University of Mumbai and a doctorate at Heidelberg. He was Professor of Sanskrit and Arts Dean at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Honorary Secretary of BORI.

Ramesh Chandra Majumdar (1888–1980) was a scholar of Indology and history who completed his dissertation at the University of Calcutta. He was a professor and vice chancellor at the University of Dhaka and served as president of the Asiatic Society.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. In 1967, he was department head at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest University, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State University.

Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where he was attested in 2015 studying under supervisors Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina.

Ramkrishna Bhattacharya (1947–2022) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Calcutta from around 1964 to 1970 and served on the faculty at Ananda Mohan College from around 1972 to 2007.
Ramon Prats is a scholar of Tibetology. He held posts attested at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources in 1999 and at Pompeu Fabra University in 2017.
Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied under teacher Steven D. Goodman and completed his doctoral studies under the supervision of Richard K. Payne.

Randy J. LaPolla (born 1955) is a linguist and sinologist who studied under James Alan Matisoff at UC Berkeley. He served as professor at the City University of Hong Kong and later held a post at Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai.

Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha. He also studied under the traditional teacher Attaragama Gnanawimala.

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught numerous students, including Chögyam Trungpa and Pema Chödrön.

Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Mario Praz, and served as Professor of Indology at the University of Rome from 1964 to 2000.
Raoul Birnbaum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He held an attested post as Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of California, Santa Cruz, in 2003 and 2017.
Raphael Kühner (1802–1878) was a German linguist. He was educated at Ernestinum Gotha and the University of Göttingen (circa 1821–1824), and he taught Georg Bühler.

Raphael von Koeber (1848–1923) was a philosopher. He studied at the Moscow Conservatory and the universities of Jena and Heidelberg, and held a post at the University of Tokyo starting in 1893, where he taught Masaharu Anesaki.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indologist and historian. He studied under R. D. Ranade at Fergusson College, and later under Sukhlal Sanghvi and Muni Jinvijaya. He served as professor at Gujarat Vidyapith and president of Gujarati Sahitya Parishad.

Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) was a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Copenhagen, he later served there as librarian and professor of literary history and Eastern languages.
Ratna Vajra Rinpoche (born 1974) is a scholar and practitioner of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, whom he succeeded in 2017.
